clauses.reason: The order amends paragraph 8 of Executive Order No. 10129 "to read as follows": "The Commission shall cease to exist at the end of May 31,1951." That text is a fixed sunset in the order's own terms. The Commission ceased to exist at the end of May 31, 1951, so the clause ended on that date. No held later order extends, revokes or restates the sunset. State on 2026-10-14: terminated.

The correction fixes the clause span to the operative sentence and quoted paragraph.

research_rationale:
EO 10236 (16 FR 3607; signed April 26, 1951; F.R. Doc. 51-4979) amends paragraph 8 of Executive Order No. 10129 of June 3, 1950, establishing the President's Commission on Migratory Labor, to read: "8. The Commission shall cease to exist at the end of May 31,1951." Identity: the census register title for this number is 'Establishing the President's Commission on Migratory Labor', which is the subject of the order amended; the Federal Register heading of the held page reads 'Amendment of Executive Order No. 10129 of June 3, 1950, Establishing the President's Commission on Migratory Labor', and the order number, the date April 26, 1951 and the document number agree with the register row. The command is a sunset: the amended paragraph ends the Commission's existence at the end of May 31, 1951, which is the first end by the order's own terms. The text says 'at the end of May 31,1951', so the end is the close of that day and the exclusive reading does not arise.
